_note: Every fact about the supplier this radar runs for. Copy to config/client.json (git-ignored) and edit; with no client.json this example is used, so the engine runs out of the box. Nothing here is a secret - secrets live in the environment.

business.name: Greenfield Produce
business.headline: peeled garlic up to 1,000 kg/day, broccoli, capsicum, exotic and regular vegetables

capacity._note: What the supplier can actually fill. A requirement he cannot serve is not a better lead for being bigger. headlineCommodity gets its own ceiling because it is the line he is set up for.

cities._note: bbox = [south, west, north, east] in WGS84 degrees. agmarknetState must match the state name data.gov.in uses, not the one you would write. aliases lists the other names the city is written under - a newspaper writes Bangalore as often as Bengaluru, and the publisher-feed lane matches every name listed here.

catalogue._note: What the supplier sells, and the Agmarknet commodity name each item is priced from. Verified against live data.gov.in records on 2026-09-11. commodity: null means Agmarknet carries no mandi line for that item - the price sheet says 'no mandi quote' rather than guessing one. approx: true means the item is priced off a nearby line (zucchini off squash), and the price sheet marks it with a ~.

keywords._note: What makes a notice, a tender row or a bid worth opening. Matched case-insensitively on word boundaries - 'mess' anchored, or it matches inside 'message'.

signals._note: How the publisher-feed and openings lanes tier a news item before anything is fetched. A produce word next to a `procurement` word is a requirement_candidate: the article is read and the model is asked. An `opening` word next to a `venue` word is awareness: the item is kept as a signal and nothing is fetched or spent on it. `near` is how many characters apart the two halves may sit and still count as one statement. Every list here is optional - left empty, the engine's own lists in src/lib/profile.mjs are used, because a tender is a tender whoever is bidding.

openers._note: The line the owner reads out. One per segment, plus the two kinds that already know what to say. Plain, factual, no claim the supplier cannot back. The model rewrites these only when it has a concrete fact to put in line one; these are the floor and they are always correct.

bySegment.wholesale: Do you buy peeled garlic in bulk?
bySegment.hotel: Daily peeled garlic and vegetables. Rates?
bySegment.caterer: Peeled garlic and vegetables for events.
bySegment.institution: We can quote for your vegetable supply.
bySegment.other: We supply fresh vegetables daily. Rates?

openers.requirementFallback: We can quote for your posted requirement.
openers.registration: You buy {what} - can we register as a supplier?
openers.registrationFallback: Can we register as a supplier?

excludeSegments._note: Listings that identify themselves as one of these are dropped during normalisation, and no copy this project generates uses the wording. Each entry is a regular expression source, matched case-insensitively against the trading name and the listing's own tags.
